en: Moso bamboo can grow up to 91 centimeters in a single day, making it one of the fastest-growing plants on Earth.
The Australian wombat produces cube-shaped feces to stop the droppings from rolling away when marking its territory.
Human stomach acid is so strong that it can dissolve metal objects like razor blades within a few hours.
Adult butterflies use specialized sensory receptors on their feet to taste the leaves where they will lay their eggs.
Trees in a forest communicate and share nutrients through a vast underground network of symbiotic fungi called mycorrhizae.
The Mexican axolotl can completely regenerate its lost limbs, spinal cord, heart, and even parts of its brain.
A mild fever helps the human body fight infections by creating an environment too hot for bacteria to survive.
An octopus has three hearts and nine brains, including a central brain and a mini-brain in each arm.
The Venus flytrap counts how many times an insect touches its trigger hairs before snapping shut to trap live prey.
If you uncoiled all the DNA inside a single human cell, it would stretch about two meters long.
Honeybees perform a figure-eight waggle dance to communicate the exact distance and direction of nectar sources to their hive mates.
The hummingbird is the only bird capable of flying backwards and hovering in mid-air by beating its wings in a figure-eight pattern.
